package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a highly obfuscated backdoor in the liblzma library, which is loaded by OpenSSH (sshd) on affected systems. This backdoor allows remote attackers with a specific private key to execute arbitrary code or bypass SSH authentication before the authentication step, effectively granting full control over the victim machine. The malicious code is deeply embedded, evades standard code review, and is triggered only under attacker-controlled conditions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated M4 macros and disguised test files containing prebuilt malicious object code, extracted and injected into liblzma during build.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build-time, the build-to-host.m4 macro extracts a disguised object file from test data and injects it into the liblzma build, resulting in a modified library with malicious hooks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting prebuilt object code from disguised test files into a production library is highly abnormal and bypasses source-level review.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal builds should only use source code and legitimate test files, not extract and inject hidden binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; test files should never be used to inject code into production binaries.
key_indicators: Extraction of object code from test files
Injection of code into core library

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when liblzma is loaded by sshd/OpenSSH)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious hook on RSA_public_decrypt function in liblzma, examining the RSA modulus and decrypting attacker-controlled payloads using ChaCha20 and Ed448 signature verification.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C (compiled to binary, injected into liblzma)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when OpenSSH calls RSA_public_decrypt, the malicious hook inspects the RSA modulus sent by the client. If the modulus matches attacker criteria, it decrypts a payload using a hardcoded ChaCha20 key, verifies an Ed448 signature, and executes attacker-supplied commands (including shell commands) before authentication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting cryptographic functions to execute attacker-supplied code is a classic backdoor technique, especially when triggered by non-standard cryptographic input.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: liblzma should not hook or alter cryptographic routines in OpenSSH, nor execute code based on SSH client input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; cryptographic hooks should never be used for command execution.
key_indicators: Use of hardcoded symmetric and asymmetric keys
Execution of shell commands from cryptographic input

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when attacker sends crafted SSH connection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Decrypted payload contains a NULL-terminated shell command string (e.g., cat /etc/shadow) that is passed directly to system() for execution.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after signature verification, the decrypted payload is interpreted as a shell command and executed with the privileges of the sshd process, allowing arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing arbitrary shell commands from cryptographic payloads is a hallmark of remote code execution backdoors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate code should execute shell commands based on SSH cryptographic handshake data.
key_indicators: Direct use of system() on attacker-supplied data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when attacker sends crafted SSH connection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Command 0x01 in the backdoor logic triggers SSH authentication bypass, allowing login with any password.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, if the attacker sends a payload with command 0x01, the backdoor bypasses SSH authentication, granting access regardless of password.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing authentication is a direct violation of security boundaries and is only seen in backdoors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Authentication routines should never be bypassed based on cryptographic handshake data.

attack_chain.action: Malicious object code is extracted from disguised test files and injected into liblzma during the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: liblzma library is now backdoored and ready to be loaded by dependent applications.

attack_chain.action: When OpenSSH (sshd) loads the malicious liblzma, the backdoor hook is active in process memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor is now able to intercept cryptographic operations in SSH connections.

attack_chain.action: Attacker connects to SSH and sends a specially crafted RSA public key modulus, triggering the backdoor logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor decrypts and verifies attacker-supplied payload.

attack_chain.action: If the payload is valid, the backdoor either executes arbitrary shell commands or bypasses SSH authentication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution or unauthorized SSH access (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: liblzma or xz-utils build process extracting object code from test files
liblzma hooking cryptographic functions (e.g., RSA_public_decrypt) in dependent processes
Execution of shell commands from within liblzma during SSH handshake
SSH authentication bypass triggered by cryptographic input
file_indicators: liblzma.so with unexpected binary differences from official source
network_indicators: SSH connections with non-standard RSA modulus values (first 16 bytes trigger backdoor)
SSH handshake traffic containing ChaCha20-encrypted payloads
Unusual SSH logins without valid authentication
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for xz-utils/liblzma versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. Analyze build logs for extraction of object code from test files. Inspect liblzma.so for unexpected binary sections or hooks on cryptographic functions. Monitor SSHD for authentication bypass or execution of shell commands during handshake. Use YARA rules to detect hardcoded keys or suspicious strings (e.g., yolAbejyiejuvnup=Evjtgvsh5okmkAvj, Shutdown) in liblzma binaries. Monitor for SSH connections with unusual RSA modulus patterns.
